maria: Quick update — ran a long TP 8-node (2x4) job with nvtx, perf and the runtime tracer. Seeing recurring all-reduce latency spikes at the same cadence as KV cache flush events. spikes ~10-40ms added, happens when per-rank message sizes fall into the 1-4KB range.

ajay: Can you paste the top of the trace or a flame?

maria: pasted short trace excerpt below (nvtx timeline + annotations). you can see repeated small allreduce calls interleaved with compute. The KV cache eviction events line up.

maria: ```
# nvprof / runtime-trace simplified
step 170: compute 28ms -> allreduce start -> 2.1KB -> nccl ring handshake 0.8ms -> allreduce kernel 1.2ms -> done
step 171: compute 27ms -> allreduce start -> 3.7KB -> nccl setup 0.9ms -> allreduce 1.4ms
...
KV_CACHE: flush @ step 170,172
```

sam: Interesting. Did you repro with nccl-tests? ring vs tree microbench?

maria: Yes. Ran all_reduce_perf across the same topology. For 2KB messages: ring p99=24ms, tree p99=17ms. For 64KB messages: ring p99=8ms, tree p99=11ms. So tradeoff flips with msg size.

linda: That matches expectation: tree reduces latency for tiny messages due to lower hop count but adds overhead for larger payloads.

ajay: Could kernel selector or batching be misrouting? We recently landed a fallback that prefers ring for high-seq runs, might be flipping incorrectly for the small-message burst.

maria: Exactly — the selector heuristic uses median seq length over a window; when KV cache flush creates a short burst, median doesn't move fast enough, so we end up using ring and pay the p99 tail.

sam: Two mitigation ideas: (1) microbatch coalescing to aggregate small allreduce payloads inside the runtime before they hit NCCL, (2) make selector sensitive to recent small-message rate (exponential decay).

linda: Low-risk quick fix: add a small coalescing window BATCHER_COALESCE_MS=2 for TP-only paths. We tried that in a canary — reduced small-message count by ~70% and p99 dropped to ~9ms on the full job.

maria: Canary commands we used: ```
export BATCHER_COALESCE_MS=2
export KVCACHE_EVICT_AGG=1
mpirun -np 8 ./all_reduce_perf -b 2K -f 2 -g 1
```

perf-bot: perf alert: canary run (maria/2024-11-02) p99 improved 24ms -> 9ms, cost delta +0.3% CPU.

ajay: For a more robust solution, we should update kernel-selector: add a short-term window (last N steps) weight so selector can prefer tree when recent small-message fraction > 30%. Also add a metric to the console: "small_msg_fraction" per route.

sam: We found an edge case: when kvcache eviction aligns across ranks, coalescing helps but only if coalesce is coordinated per-slice. If ranks independently coalesce, you still get imbalanced message sizes and NCCL handshake overhead. We need deterministic coalesce boundaries.

linda: Proposal: implement leader-driven micro-coalesce: one rank emits coalesce boundaries via a tiny control packet (fits into existing control channel) so all ranks flush at same boundary. Low overhead.

maria: I'll open a PR with the Batcher change + selector tweak + perf dashboard metric. Plan: canary on staging 10% of TP clusters, monitor p99 and small_msg_fraction for 48h, then roll 100% if no regressions.

ajay: Also add nccl env experiment flags to the test harness so we can force tree/ring for AB testing (nccl algorithm override per-run). That will help verify selector quality before rollout.

sam: TL;DR: root cause = KV-cache aligned evictions creating short-message allreduce bursts; fix = coordinated micro-coalescing + fast-reacting kernel selector + observability.

linda: :thumbsup: thanks. Maria — can you assign owners and ETA in the PR?

maria: Yep — PR in 30m, owners: @sam (coalesce), @ajay (selector), @linda (canary), ETA EOW for initial canary.

maria: I'll drop the raw traces and nccl-tests results to the thread in a follow-up message.
